pairs.difference: A: the bracelet runs from hot pink to orange with yellow-orange charms. It is loud, but it has one clear pink-orange family against the cyan rings. B: the Saturn body is orange with cream bands, and the ring is cream with a pink line. In the lens the cream reads as a pale greyish wash, and the whole planet is pulled warm cream and orange. This matches the generated cards in the lessons, which turn neutrals into cream. A's subject chroma is above the real range, so this call is weak.
pairs.fix: Paint the planet's light bands as cool off-white with a slight blue-grey shade instead of cream. Make the ring pale grey-lilac and the orange a slightly deeper rust that darkens to a red-brown in shadow.

pairs.difference: A: the seahorse is orange with a yellow belly and a green eye on a deep blue water gradient, with a clear hero-versus-background hue split. B: the sand, castle and shadows are all one warm sand-orange mass. A saturated lime bucket and a blue shovel are dropped on top as extra pure hues, giving about 6 hue families, above the real range. The castle's shadows stay orange-brown instead of turning cooler.
pairs.fix: Cool the sand shadows to a muted grey-violet. Keep the castle a lighter, cooler beige than the beach. Tone the bucket to a softer green, so the card rests on fewer, calmer colors.

pairs.difference: A: a flat pure-green burst background with almost no warm or neutral area, about 1.5 hue families, below the real range. It holds a pure yellow cube and pure blue panels, and the shadows on the green stay fully saturated. B: a crimson ring box with a deep wine shadow side, a beige interior, a gold coin and cyan rays. Its shadows shift to a related darker red, as on real cards.
pairs.fix: Make the background green less neon, with darker, cooler rays toward the corners. Give the satellite body a warm grey-metal frame with only a gold panel. Let the cube's shadow side drop to an olive-brown instead of staying bright yellow.

pairs.difference: A is the real computer card: cool grey-white plastic, a warm desk, an orange backdrop, and violet-grey shadows on the keyboard. B: the rover and the ground are almost colorless grey, with a subject chroma of 0.01, far below the real range. The orange sky is the only hue, so nearly all of the warm share comes from the background. There is no local color on the hero apart from a tiny blue lens.
pairs.fix: Give the rover a clear local color, such as white panels with orange or blue trim. Tint the moon ground a dusty warm-grey with violet shadows so the hero and ground carry related color.

pairs.difference: A: the white plane has blue belly shadows and blue windows on a blue sky. It is all one cool family, and its shadow chroma runs high. B: the UFO's grey metal saucer goes almost neutral, and in the lens it melts into the sky blue. Glowing yellow bulbs and a mint-green dome are the only accents. The hero has less local color than the sky, which is the opposite of real cards. Low confidence: A is also very monochrome.
pairs.fix: Give the saucer a colored metal, such as a teal or lilac hull with warm brass rivets. Keep the dome a clear pale cyan so the ship separates from the sky by hue, not just by grey.

pairs.difference: A: the map has sky-blue sea, cream land, green islands and a red-brown compass on orange wood. It uses several natural local colors with cream neutrals between them. B: the card is reduced to two masses, a saturated navy disc and orange wood. Only an orange planet accent repeats the wood hue, and there is no neutral resting color.
pairs.fix: Add a muted metal rim to the star chart in a warm brass or grey. Make the inner disc a deep blue with a slight teal variation, and soften the wood to a less saturated tan.

pairs.difference: A is the real drum card: blue shells, gold hardware, and a magenta-violet stage with related deep wine shadows. B: the brick posts, the metal gate and the paving are all red-orange and salmon. The shadows on the bricks and gate stay orange-red. Only the green lawn and the sky break up a card that is pulled warm.
pairs.fix: Paint the gate as dark wrought iron, charcoal with a slight blue sheen, instead of copper. Cool the paving stones toward grey-beige and let the brick shadows go a deeper maroon-violet.

pairs.difference: A: a flat violet background floods the whole card. In the lens the white helmet shell becomes pink-violet and its shadows are purple, and only an orange visor and a stripe break the hue. That is about 1.7 hue families, below the real range. B: blue shoes with green, teal and pink accents on orange and cream. It is busy but has separate local colors.
pairs.fix: Keep the helmet a cool neutral white with grey-blue shadows, not lilac. Make the background a softer violet with a darker vignette, and add a small cool accent such as a blue patch or light.

pairs.difference: A: the wall, the panel frame and even the grey metal plate take on lavender. The warm share is about 0.05 and the buttons are the only warm note. The lens shows the panel's grey as violet-grey and the shadows as blue-purple. B: a green curtain, an orange wall, a cyan fan and silver metal. It keeps believable local colors, with neutral metal that stays grey.
pairs.fix: Make the control plate a true neutral steel grey with slightly warm highlights. Give the wall a muted grey-violet with some warm light from the top lamp, so the purple does not tint everything.

pairs.difference: A: a cobalt cabinet on violet, with multicolored cans and bottles inside giving several small hue accents. B: about two hue families. The pink background floods the glass flask, which reads as pink in the lens, and the only other hue is a neon lime liquid, with no neutral glass or cork shading. Both subjects are louder than the real cards, so the call is weak.
pairs.fix: Draw the flask glass as clear pale grey-blue with white edge highlights instead of pink. Make the liquid a slightly deeper yellow-green, and use a softer, darker rose background.

pairs.difference: A: a red-and-white rocket on grey concrete. In the lens the rocket's cast shadow and the window rims fall into the same saturated red mass, and the white body takes a pale blue tint. Shadow chroma is above the real range. B: a primary yellow, red and blue roller coaster, very loud. Its shadows go to a related darker red and blue, which matches how real cards handle shadow color.
pairs.fix: Paint the rocket's cast shadow as a cool blue-grey on the concrete, not reddish. Darken the shadow side of the red fins toward a deep crimson-maroon, and keep the white body a warm-neutral off-white.

pairs.difference: A: the hiker has natural local colors, with a skin tone, a blue shirt, khaki pants, a green bedroll and a desert under cyan sky. The chroma on both the subject and the background sits inside the real range. B: the cow and chicken wear silver suits that read almost grey, so the hero is muted. Meanwhile the grass and sky are louder than real cards, and orange appears on the cow's muzzle, the suit trim and the chicken. The background is louder than the subject.
pairs.fix: Give the space suits a colored base, such as pale blue or white with bold orange panels and warm cream highlights. Tone the meadow green down and make the far hills bluer, so the characters stay the most colorful part of the card.

pattern: On color, generated cards still give themselves away in three ways. They flood one background hue across the hero, so neutral greys and whites take the backdrop's tint (violet, pink, blue). They drop the hero to near-colorless grey metal while the background stays loud. They push local colors to pure primaries or a two-mass complementary split. Real cards keep cool grey-whites and deeper related shadow hues (crimson to wine, orange to rust or brown). They also leave some neutral rest areas between saturated masses.
